_comment: parkrun: ~2,965 free, weekly, volunteer-run events across 20 countries, expanded into dated occurrences over a rolling horizon. The adapter has always been wired into aggregate-events.yml and this file did not exist, so the step printed 'no parkrun_sources.json - skipping parkrun' on every run since it was written and the whole 'running' layer stayed empty.
_run_weekdays: TWO days, not one. A weekly schedule re-expands to byte-identical rows so a daily run is wasted work, but a source that runs one day a week has no retry and nothing notices - the OSM Overpass sweep lost a whole week's international market catalogue to exactly that. Monday and Thursday means a lost run costs three days rather than seven.
_start_times: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Start times are not in the feed and they vary by country and by season - a UK 9am is an Australian 7am in summer, and within the UK some events start at 9:30. The adapter emits an all-day event when a country has no entry here and puts 'Start time on the event page.' in the description, which is honest; a plausible country-wide guess would be the well-formed-and-wrong failure this repo keeps paying for. Fill a code in only after checking that country's events, and the sync will convert the naive local time using the coordinates.
_countries: parkrun's own country codes are opaque integers and the feed carries no country NAME, only a domain. This map is derived from those domains and written down as DATA rather than parsed from the TLD at runtime, because org.uk -> GB is the sort of special case that hides in a regex. Counts are live events at the time of writing.
